title: Early paired ALOHA traps limit a power-law mixture box to 2.38 mol/m2 of oxygen loss at mean inputs
abstract: We test a particle-breakdown alternative to ventilation loss at Station ALOHA. Paired 150, 300 and 500 m carbon traps from 48 cruises in 1989-1995 constrain two moments of a nonnegative power-law mixture. A continuous dual certificate gives a sharp minimum 300-700 m breakdown fraction of 0.18895 at equal-year mean inputs. With the measured annual export history and zero added deficit in 1997, any later power-law mixture and any nonnegative renewal history can give at most 2.3793 mol O2/m2 of added deficit in 2009-2024. The published oxygen loss is 4.8221, with 3.3212 after density displacement. But seven-year resampling gives a conditional capacity range of 0.845-4.383, and differential depth calibration can remove the point constraint. Thus paired early traps limit the free early mixture in a prior counterexample but do not reject changed particle breakdown as a cause. The early sample must represent the baseline. Missing carbon pathways, non-power-law profiles and transport remain open. Code, proof, aggregate evidence and input hashes are included.

display.caption: Paired early traps constrain a lower layer-breakdown fraction. The resulting point capacity stays below the published losses. Sampling and calibration uncertainty can remove this constraint.
